original.target_description: Study 1: full eligible USA sample; simple correlation between observer age and estimated age of the bistable woman.

n.exclusions: Restricted to USA respondents; required both attention checks, valid demographics, and an estimated age older than 18. Final eligible sample 393.
n.location: Method, Participants, final-sample paragraph (publisher full-text HTML)
n.quote: There were therefore 393 participants (m = 242, f = 151) from the USA in the final sample.

replication.target_description: Study 1: full eligible sample; one-tailed Pearson correlation between participant age and estimated age of ambiguous figure.

n.exclusions: 14 of 260 recruited participants excluded following eligibility checks (person and female identification), leaving 246.
n.location: Methods, Participants, first paragraph (publisher full-text HTML)
n.quote: An analysis of participants’ eligibility for inclusion (see below for criteria) resulted in the exclusion of 14 participants, reducing the final sample to N = 246.

es.location: p. 4, Results, Primary analyses: replication of original findings, first paragraph (publisher full-text HTML)

reported_success.location: p. 4, Results, Primary analyses: replication of original findings, first paragraph (publisher full-text HTML)
reported_success.quote: Similar results were obtained in the original experiment of Nicholls et al., who found a mean age difference of 6.32 years and a correlation of 0.24.

notes: Extracted the full-sample correlation, not the percept-specific or unfamiliar-only correlations. Original prints r(393); analytic n is independently documented as 393. The replication reproduces the age-estimate relationship while disputing its interpretation as a perceptual bias.
